turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, Kai Pillay's in, six years old, mom with him. I did the observations already, before you called us.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, sorry, this thing's frozen on the lab tab again. One moment. Right, what's brought him?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's burning up, and there's a cough. It started around Diwali, or just after, I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Around Diwali. And the cough itself, is it—
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wet, Doctor, and it wakes him at night. Sorry, I jumped in.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, you're fine. How many days for the fever? Say it again, I typed in the wrong box.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The fever's newer than the cough. From Monday, so five days, if I've counted properly.
[SEG0008] person_1 (NURSE): His dad at the front desk said three days, from Thursday. That's what landed on the triage note.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thursday? Ag, no. Dad's been away for work. I'm the one there. Monday, five days. Well, pretty much.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between three and five days, we won't force it. How high did it get? Repeat that, the fan just roared.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Our thermometer at home said 39 last night. His father tells everyone 40, but he never measured, I did.
[SEG0012] person_1 (NURSE): Triage just now, temperature 38.1, pulse 118, oxygen 97 percent, respiratory rate 26, blood pressure 98 over 62.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): 38.1, thanks sister. Kai, how are you today?
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): I am not feeling well, Doctor. Thank you for asking.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Shame, man. Is your throat sore?
[SEG0016] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. My throat is sore.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He said so before we left. He didn't go to school. And he's been off his food since yesterday.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Off his food. Any vomiting, or a runny tummy?
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting. There was one loose—
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hold on, this popup won't close. Say the tummy part again?
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, and no diarrhoea. I started to say a loose stool, but it was a normal one, actually.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, good. What have you given him for the fever?
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panado syrup, by mouth. One medicine spoon, the 5 ml one, every six hours, since the fever started.
[SEG0024] person_1 (NURSE): Dad told me it was Nurofen, two spoons, not Panado. I nearly charted ibuprofen instead.

[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The Panado was me. He might have given Brufen last night while I was at my sister's. He just said a spoon, I don't know if he meant one spoon or the two he told you.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Panado 5 ml six-hourly is clear. The Brufen, your amounts don't match, so I'm not writing a dose. Any allergies?
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing he's allergic to. No rash from a medicine, nothing like that.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): No known allergies. Asthma? Or has a cough like this happened before?
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No asthma. He had croup once, last winter, or the winter before, I always mix those winters. It settled at home, we didn't come in.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you pin a month on the croup? I lost the sentence, someone walked past.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I can't, Doctor. Last winter, or the one before. That's the best I can do.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll leave it undated. Anyone smoking at home?
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His dad smokes, but outside by the garage, not in the house. I've never smoked.
[SEG0034] person_4 (PATIENT): Excuse me, Doctor. May I have some water, please?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, of course. Sister will sort that now now. Kai, when you cough, does it hurt?
[SEG0036] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. It hurts.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He keeps tapping the middle of his chest when he says it. Not the tummy.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Middle of the chest. Any wheeze you've heard at home? Pulling in under the ribs?
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No wheeze. No pulling in. He does breathe fast when the fever spikes, and it eases once the Panado kicks in.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eases after the Panado. Let me listen. Big slow breaths for me, my boy.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, no crackles and no wheeze. Throat is red. Ears are fine. Tummy is soft and it doesn't hurt when I press.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Shame, that's a relief. I got myself worked up, my brother's little one had a bad chest last year. Sorry, not relevant.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's all right. My working impression is a viral infection, the fever and the cough together. I can't rule out an early pneumonia, but the chest doesn't sound like it today.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no x-ray? The lady at the chemist was pushing me to ask.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. If he's not better in three days, come back and I'll send him for a chest x-ray then.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the Panado, do I just carry on with the 5 ml spoon?

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Carry on with Panado, but make it 7.5 ml every six hours, he's six and the 5 is light. Don't add the ibuprofen until dad can say exactly what he gave, I don't want you doubling up.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): 7.5, ja, I'll mark the syringe. He'll drink if I nag him.

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Small sips of fluid through the day, and keep him home from school tomorrow. If he goes drowsy, or the breathing gets harder, come straight in, don't wait out the three days.
[SEG0050] person_1 (NURSE): I'll stick the obs in the file. Dad's still sitting in the bakkie, parking out there is hectic if you wanted him.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, leave him, we're done with the clash on the dates. Mom's account is what I'm using, we just won't pretend they match.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you, Doctor. Kai, manners.
[SEG0053] person_4 (PATIENT): Thank you very much, Doctor.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pleasure, Kai. Off you go. Sister, call the next one when the screen behaves.
